Research

Fairness and interpretability in AI.

NewPublished · Journal of High School Science, 2026

Emotion-associated representations in the feed forward gates of a language model

With Sankar Balasubramanian (Indian Institute of Science) as co-author.

Finding neurons in a language model that light up for emotions doesn’t show that they drive its emotional behaviour. I tested that gap at three levels, representation, reconfiguration and causal control, in the feed-forward gates of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. Statistically corrected activation signatures for six emotions overlapped in a structure that matches a psychological circumplex model, and partly carried over between Chinese texts and their English translations.

Across four families of tasks the signatures shifted with what the model was asked to do, but they didn’t explain its emotional behaviour on their own: the preregistered measure failed held-out validation, with two of fourteen hypotheses supported, and suppressing emotional expression showed no reliable change at the sampled position. Emotion-associated structure isn’t the same as causal control, which remains untested.

Read the paper DOI 10.64336/001c.175619 Interactive version Code and data
Published · NHSJS, April 2026Gold CREST Award

Fairness and Dependency Preservation in Synthetic Credit Data

Can synthetic data safely stand in for real data in loan approval models? I compared SMOTE, CTGAN, TVAE and Gaussian Copula on the German Credit dataset and created a Dependency Preservation Score to measure how well each kept the relationships between credit variables intact.

The finding: every synthetic method distorted those relationships and made fairness less stable, so for high-stakes decisions like lending, original data with fairness-aware preprocessing is the safer choice. The work earned a Gold CREST Award from the British Science Association.

Projects

Tech built for real people.

Live in every Indian state

AgriBridge

A multilingual Android app for Indian farmers earning under ₹10,000 a month. It helps them find nearby markets, government schemes and credit information in their own language, with a chatbot for quick questions.

I validated it with NABARD and three Farmer Producer Organisations in Karnataka, raised ₹1,23,000 to build it, and early results suggest around a 10% rise in income. AgriBridge is now available to farmers in every state in India. I presented it at the 64th UN Commission for Social Development in New York as a 1M1B Changemaker.

AndroidMultilingualChatbot
📷 Follow @project_agribridge on Instagram ↗ agribridge.rayanupadhyay.com

Mandalink

A web app for learning Mandarin through its 214 Kangxi radicals, the small building blocks inside Chinese characters. Spot the radical and you get a clue to the meaning of characters you’ve never seen. It has flashcards, quizzes, timed challenges, animated stroke-order practice, an AI radical tutor, printable writing worksheets and an IB Chinese course, with accounts, XP, badges and a leaderboard.

I’ve built it twice. The first version was one Python and Streamlit app, with AI hints through Groq and Mandarin audio from Edge text-to-speech. It hit Streamlit’s limits: every click reran the whole script, pages had no real URLs, and nothing else could talk to it. So I rewrote it from scratch as a React front end on a Java Spring Boot REST API with PostgreSQL, which is what runs at mandalink.org today. Its announcement board also feeds the news on this site.

    What others say

    Try the idea

    A toy version of the question in my paper: does synthetic data keep the relationships between variables, and does fairness stay stable?

    Toy illustration. This uses a small made-up dataset generated in your browser and simplified stand-in generators, not the German Credit data, the real methods or the paper's score. For the real results, read the paper.

    How I built this site

    The whole site is one HTML file with no build step. The 3D room, Mandalink island, the rooftop and Bangalore are drawn with Three.js, and every model (the furniture, the creatures, the weapons, the city) is built from simple shapes in code rather than downloaded. Sound effects are generated live with the Web Audio API, progress is saved in your browser, and other visitors show up as ghosts through a small public message relay. There is a simple version for screen readers and keyboards, a reduce-effects setting for slower devices, and I test it with a headless browser.
